problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ k \\ 10\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Column Space of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Value of an Unknown Given a Vector That’s in the Column Space of a Matrix

examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(A),$ then the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 3 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2+k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & -8 & -32 \\ 5 & -1 & 2+k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & -8 & -32 \\ 0 & -11 & k-48\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -11 & k-48\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+11{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=10 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ 0=k-4.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-4,$ which means that $k=4.$

feedback.problem:
The matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(A).$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2}$ are the respective columns of $A.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}\,\,-4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ we need to check if the equation $Ax=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & \,\,-4 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 & 2 \\ \,\,-1 & \,\,-1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & \,\,-4 \\ 0 & \,\,2 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & \,\,-4 \\ 0 & \,\,2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 2{x}_{2}=-6 \\ 0=1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the false statement $0=1.$ 

Therefore, the system is inconsistent, which implies that $b\notin \text{Col}(A).$
